statement: A column holding a single value carries no variation any model can use, so it is settled as excluded without asking.
claimed_basis: "a constant has no variation for any model to use" (KIND_RULES role:excluded, readings.py:1172).

statement: Under the genomics or metabolomics lens, a block of at least 20 numeric non-outcome, non-identifier, non-acquisition columns is unnormalized (needs a normalization before modeling) if, for counts, at least 20 of them are non-negative whole numbers with more than two distinct values reaching a maximum of at least 100 (genomics lens), or, for intensities, they are non-negative and their positive values span at least 100-fold and either reach at least 1,000 or have median per-feature skewness of at least 0.5 (metabolomics lens); values failing these tests are treated as already normalized or log-scale.
regime: genomics or metabolomics lens; >=20 assay-like numeric columns; read from values only, outcome never consulted, before the split
decision: whether the omics_scale finding is raised, which arms the refusal of linear families and the normalization question
claimed_basis: Constants commented in code (omics.py:64-68): 'log2 intensities stay below ~40', 'raw intensities reach thousands', 'unlogged concentrations are right-skewed (a log-normal feature with a 30% CV has skewness near 1); log-scale ones are not'; genotype dosages 0/1/2 excluded by COUNT_MAX. No citation.

statement: The same kind of measurement taken at baseline beside an outcome measured over follow-up (HbA1c beside incident diabetes, blood pressure beside incident hypertension, LDL beside LDL at 12 months) precedes the outcome, can predict it, and may have changed or been changed by the diet, so it takes the declared with-and-without pair rather than being left out; beside a change-since-baseline outcome, adjusting for a baseline the exposure may have changed can itself bias the analysis, so neither model alone is the default.
regime: Inference with a follow-up outcome (time-to-event, incident binary, or follow-up/change/time-since-baseline outcome); covariate of the outcome's group.
decision: Pre-filled adjustment answers (with-and-without pair) for a baseline level of the outcome's kind.
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §08; Schisterman 2009; Glymour et al. 2005 Am J Epidemiol 162:267-278 (baseline adjustment in change analyses); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 3.

statement: For tuning XGBoost under prediction, the search box learning rate [0.01, 0.3] (log), depth [2, 10], min child weight [1, 64] rows-equivalent (log), row share [0.5, 1], column share per tree [0.3, 1], L2 λ [1e-3, 100] (log), rounds [25, 1,000] (only without early stopping), with α=0, tree booster and hist fixed, contains the well-performing settings.
decision: XGBoost's declared search space and fixed settings
claimed_basis: Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019 (λ 2^[−10, 10]; child weight 2^[0, 7]); Chen & Guestrin 2016 / XGBoost tuning notes; RECIPES §4.1 ("conventions, narrowed").

statement: A gain of 0.01 on the primary metric's own scale (baseline.MIN_GAIN) is the smallest gain that matters for every task, including the mean squared error of a numeric outcome in its squared outcome units, log loss in nats, the ranked probability score and the Brier score at a horizon, so a gain below 0.01 is 'too small to matter whatever the folds say'.
regime: Prediction; every task; the verdict reads PRIMARY[task] (regression: mse, binary/multiclass: log_loss, ordinal: rps, time to event: brier_t)
decision: The 'better' threshold in the baseline verdict; also the equivalence margin δ = MIN_GAIN/2 of the T1 nested-tuning test and the STRATIFICATION_OPTIMISM argument
claimed_basis: 'a convention, not a cited rule' (baseline.py:25-27); STRATIFICATION_OPTIMISM §5 and RECIPES §8 T1 reuse it as 'the app's smallest meaningful gain'.

statement: With a log or a nonlinear form of a substituted energy component, moving k kcal no longer has one effect per kcal. Each person's effect depends on k and their own intake, so each point of the substitution curve is an average over the analyzed rows at that k, not a coefficient difference. An all-components contrast is undefined on logged components.
regime: substitution curve with log or spline on donor or recipient
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 Corrected ("Draft 1 said 'ratio rather than difference'; that was wrong")

statement: Values filled before the table was made by an unrecorded method are read as missing and re-imputed in each training fold at the median without indicators, because their missingness belongs to the upstream process, not the person, and does not exist at the moment of use.
regime: prediction; provider-imputed values flagged in the table

statement: Under Predict with a period held out, R² on the opened period computed against that period's own mean is conventional and conservative, and the comparison with a deployable baseline is the RMSE against the development mean's RMSE.
regime: prediction; a sealed latest period (NHANES glucose capture)
decision: the opened cycle's R² in Results

statement: For clustering, a column with exactly two distinct values (e.g. a 0/1 code) is a category, not an amount.
claimed_basis: docstring ("a 0/1 code is a category, not an amount")

statement: Under Estimate, relabeling a two-valued column that is a declared modifier of the exposure (in an exposure × modifier interaction), coding its two spellings the other way round, leaves the exposure's main coefficient and its interval exactly unchanged and only flips the sign of the modifier's own coefficient and the interaction term, so the repair needs no post-lock check.
regime: estimation with a two-valued covariate that is a declared modifier (in an interaction with the exposure)
claimed_basis: materiality_calibration.json 'invariance' entry; SURFACING_POLICY §2.6; Frisch–Waugh–Lovell (Frisch & Waugh 1933; Lovell 1963).

statement: For NHANES data the correct survey weight is the weight of the largest sample on which any analysis variable was measured — the MEC examination weight whenever an examination variable is in the model, even when a fasting analyte such as glucose is also analyzed — because it keeps the most participants and so gives the most precise estimate.
regime: NHANES analyses combining exam, fasting-subsample and dietary variables

statement: Each cross-validated score's standard error, and the interval for each pair of families' difference (the corrected repeated k-fold t over at least 10 × K folds), computed on the user's rows, tell whether two models differ, in place of a rule about sample size.
